keys.default: (unset — no store backing: in-store workspace mounts are not bound)
keys.description: what backs the agent workspace store on the substrate — a host path or named volume (docker backend), the PVC claim name (k8s backend); the process backend shares the filesystem and needs none. The RUNTIME's own value: a workload spec's VEXA_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_* keys are discarded, and this is injected into every spec that declares a mount set. `emptyDir:` = the s3 workspace backend: nothing backs the store on the substrate; a k8s worker gets a private emptyDir at the target and a docker worker its own filesystem, and hydrates its mounts from agent-api

where the workspace store sits inside a workload (agent-api's VEXA_WORKSPACES_DIR). Every mount a spec declares must sit strictly under it, or the create is refused (400); on the process backend it is also the root the POSIX tenant isolation seals
s3 workspace backend on k8s: the sizeLimit of a worker's emptyDir workspace cache (e.g. 2Gi)

keys.default: (unset — no out-of-store mount source is served)
keys.description: comma-separated absolute host paths, outside the workspace store, that a workload's mount set may name as a mount source; any other source is refused. Compose and Helm set it to agent-api's separately managed _global tier when an operator configures one
grace (s) a stopping workload gets between SIGTERM and force-kill

keys.default: (chart's global.tolerations, JSON — the runtime's own tolerations)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of toleration objects stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod (not a Deployment child) tolerates the same taints the runtime does — else it strands Pending forever on an all-tainted pool (#673). Empty [] ⇒ no tolerations; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (a silently dropped constraint is the bug)

keys.default: [] (no Secret is mounted into any workload)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON array of {secret, file, mountPath} — one named key of an operator Secret mounted read-only (subPath) into every spawned AGENT WORKER Pod, for a harness that reads a subscription file (codex: auth.json). Never a meeting bot. Each entry must name its key: a whole Secret is refused, and so is a key that is a model-provider API key, VEXA_MODEL_SECRET_*, VEXA_MODEL_PROXY_SECRET or INTERNAL_API_SECRET (H5/W1: those live with agent-api and the model proxy alone). The key's content is checked too: an init container reads each mounted key before the worker starts and stops the Pod when it holds a model-provider API key (an sk- key other than an Anthropic subscription's OAuth tokens) or a non-empty value for one of those names (a codex auth.json in API-key mode). A refused or malformed entry fails the spawn. Helm: runtime.workerSecretMounts, which also refuses the chart's own Secret and a model catalog's Secrets at render

keys.default: (chart's global.nodeSelector, JSON — the runtime's own nodeSelector)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node-label selectors stamped onto every SPAWNED Pod's spec so a bare `kubectl run` bot/agent Pod schedules onto the same pool the runtime does. Empty {} ⇒ no selector; malformed JSON is fatal at spawn (#673)

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares. runtime.v1 carries one value per dimension, so it sets BOTH the container's request and its limit (Guaranteed QoS) — the declaration a namespace ResourceQuota admits on (#1005) — unless RUNTIME_BOT_CPU_LIMIT sets a higher limit. Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared (the pre-#1005 unbounded spawn); a non-numeric value, or one between 0 and 0.001 (it would be declared 0m), is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot CPU limit equals RUNTIME_BOT_CPU)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU limit (cores) of every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod, above its RUNTIME_BOT_CPU request, so a bot bursts onto a node's idle cores while the scheduler still packs on the request. The Pod's QoS becomes Burstable. Must be a positive number no lower than RUNTIME_BOT_CPU, which must be set; anything else is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the meeting-bot class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. A HARD ceiling — a bot exceeding it is OOM-killed mid-meeting — so size it for real meetings, not for the smallest node. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no cpu, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: CPU cores every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Sized INDEPENDENTLY of the meeting bot — a code harness is not a browser — so an operator can right-size each class alone (#1005). Unset/empty ⇒ no cpu declared; a non-numeric value, or one between 0 and 0.001 (it would be declared 0m), is fatal at boot

keys.default: (unset — the agent-worker class declares no memory, preserving runtime.v1's optional resources)
keys.description: k8s backend: memory (MiB) every SPAWNED agent-worker Pod declares, as BOTH request and limit. Unset/empty ⇒ no memory declared; a non-numeric value is fatal at boot (#1005)

keys.default: (unset — meeting-bot Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR)
keys.description: k8s backend: JSON object of node labels every SPAWNED meeting-bot Pod selects. When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_NODE_SELECTOR for this class only, so bots can run on their own pool. Read and validated at boot (label keys and values per Kubernetes' rules); malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — meeting-bot Pods take the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS)

When set it replaces the runtime-wide RUNTIME_K8S_TOLERATIONS for this class only. Validated at boot; malformed is fatal at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

keys.default: (unset — no priorityClassName, the cluster's default priority)

Validated at boot (a plain relative path). Never taken from a workload spec

k8s backend: a Localhost seccomp profile every SPAWNED agent-worker container runs under instead of RuntimeDefault, as a path relative to the kubelet's seccomp root. Validated at boot. Never taken from a workload spec

k8s backend: true lets a spawned Pod's tolerations (runtime-wide or per class) include one with no key (it tolerates every taint) or one for a control-plane or system taint (node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, node-role.kubernetes.io/master, CriticalAddonsOnly). Off, such a value is refused at boot

k8s backend: boot re-adoption also takes Pods with runtime.managed=true and NO runtime.instance label, i.e. bots a 0.12 runtime spawned that are still in a meeting across the upgrade (find/stop already treat them as this runtime's). Without it meeting-api sees those live bots as untracked and fails their meetings after the escalation window. false = adopt only this instance's Pods

k8s backend: which runtime this is (the chart sets the Helm release name). Every Pod it spawns carries it as the label runtime.instance, and boot re-adoption selects on it, so two releases in one namespace never adopt each other's Pods

keys.default: (unset — spawned Pods trust the image's own roots only)
keys.description: k8s backend: corporate TLS inspection. JSON {"configMap" | "secret": <name>, "key": <key holding the PEM root CA>, "awsCaBundle": <bool>} (the chart sets it from global.extraCA). Every SPAWNED bot and agent-worker Pod then mounts the PEM read-only, runs an init container that writes its image's system bundle plus the PEM into an emptyDir, and gets SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO (and AWS_CA_BUNDLE unless awsCaBundle is false) pointing at it, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and VEXA_EXTRA_CA_FILE at the PEM; the bot imports the PEM into Chromium's NSS store. A key the workload already sets wins. Validated at boot; malformed is fatal. Never taken from a workload spec

DOCKER-HOST path (NOT an in-container path) to a claude credentials JSON (~/.claude/.credentials.json); the docker backend bind-mounts it READ-ONLY into every spawned agent-worker at /root/.claude/.credentials.json — the claude-code runner's subscription credential path, read only by the official claude CLI (a consumer subscription is never moved into the model proxy; every API key is, and reaches no worker: H5/W1). compose also mirror-mounts it into the runtime container at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude-credentials so the config.v1 file probe can verify the host file actually exists (docker turns a MISSING host path into an empty directory in the worker → 'Model inference failed: Not logged in'). PAIR IT WITH HOST_CLAUDE_DIR: this single-FILE mirror is pinned to the inode it was created with, so it goes stale the moment the CLI refreshes the token

keys.default: (unset — only the legacy single-file mirror is available)
keys.description: DOCKER-HOST path of the claude config DIRECTORY (~/.claude), mirror-mounted READ-ONLY into the long-lived runtime + agent-api containers at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude. Same credential as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS, delivered in the shape that SURVIVES A TOKEN REFRESH: the CLI replaces .credentials.json via rename(2) (a NEW inode), and a single-FILE bind stays pinned to the inode it was created with, so a long-lived container reads the pre-refresh token until it is recreated (32h of 'Not logged in' on the dogfood stack, 2026-08-31). A DIRECTORY bind resolves the filename live. Set it to the parent of HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS

DOCKER-HOST path to Codex subscription auth (~/.codex/auth.json); mounted read-only into spawned agent workers at /tmp/.codex/auth.json (WORKER_CODEX_HOME), or copied to ~/.codex/auth.json in a process-backend child's private HOME
